title: Career classifier bake-off: Gemini discovery extractor vs Jev
notes: Decision instrument for adding TypeSafe's Jev classifier to career classification (2026-10-13). Manual tier with no floors: it informs one owner decision and gates nothing. The Gemini arm runs the production extractDiscoverySignals with its real prompt; the Jev arm asks two Choice questions over the same last-10 message window, twice, the second time with every option list reversed (Jev's docs say it favors the first option), so jev_order_flip_rate measures that bias. Information parity: on national clusters both arms see the 14 names only; on SPOKES pathways the extractor prompt lists ids only while Jev gets each pathway's production label and description, which is how Jev would be deployed. A failed case (empty or all-zero extraction, a thrown error, or a refused Jev call) counts as wrong in every top-1 ratio. Fixture is synthetic, written by an AI agent from a written labeling rule (the rule is what an instructor should audit), 32 English cases with Spanish pairs; Spanish rows await native-speaker review. TYPESAFE_API_KEY is optional: without it the Jev metrics are null with a skipped note and the Gemini baseline still runs. Per-case predictions land in reports/benchmarks/career-classifier/<timestamp>.json. Never point this suite at real student conversations: scripts/bench/suites/lib/typesafe-client.mjs bypasses the AI resolver, audit log and de-identification on purpose.
